channel.description: Nature is the foremost international weekly scientific journal in the world and is the flagship journal for Nature Portfolio. It publishes the finest peer-reviewed research in all fields of science and technology on the basis of its originality, importance, interdisciplinary interest, timeliness, accessibility, elegance and surprising conclusions. Nature publishes landmark papers, award winning news, leading comment and expert opinion on important, topical scientific news and events that enable readers to share the latest discoveries in science and evolve the discussion amongst the global scientific community.

item.title: [8] Parity-dependent coupling of molecular spin chains to a superconductor
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Diego Peña, Jose Ignacio Pascual

Authors: Katerina Vaxevani, Jon Ortuzar, Stefano Trivini, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: STM/STS on molecular spin chains coupled to superconductors; relevant to Majorana physics.

Tags: #STM/STS #superconductivity #molecularchains #spinchains #Majoranaphysics

Abstract: Scanning tunnelling spectroscopy shows that the fractional spin-1/2 end states of molecular Haldane chains couple differently to a superconducting condensate depending on whether the chain contains an even or odd number of spin-1 triangulene units.

item.title: [7] Clasping folds enable superior elastic strength of graphene films
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Zhiping Xu, Chao Gao

Authors: Lidan Wang, Yangchao Liao, Jingjie Huang, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Graphene films and their mechanical properties are relevant as a 2D material.

Tags: #graphene #2Dmaterials #mechanicalproperties

Abstract: Two-dimensional graphene films with unusual folded surfaces are synthesized through a modular assembly strategy and show enhanced strength, toughness and elastic strain owing to stress distribution between interlayer folds.
